title: Psalms Chapter 98 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 98 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 98 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 98.

questions.question: Why are we instructed to sing a new song unto the LORD in Psalms 98:1?
options: Because he hath done marvellous things
Because the earth is full of beauty
Because the heavens declare his glory
questions.correctAnswer: Because he hath done marvellous things
questions.explanation: Psalms 98:1 says to sing unto the LORD a new song because he hath done marvellous things.

questions.question: What has the LORD's right hand and holy arm gotten for Him according to Psalms 98:1?
questions.correctAnswer: Victory
questions.explanation: Psalms 98:1 states that his right hand and holy arm hath gotten him the victory.

questions.question: What has the LORD made known according to Psalms 98:2?
questions.correctAnswer: His salvation
questions.explanation: Psalms 98:2 says the LORD hath made known his salvation.

questions.question: To whom has the LORD openly shewed his righteousness according to Psalms 98:2?
questions.correctAnswer: The heathen
questions.explanation: Psalms 98:2 mentions that his righteousness hath he openly shewed in the sight of the heathen.

questions.question: According to Psalms 98:3, what has the LORD remembered toward the house of Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: His mercy and truth
questions.explanation: Psalms 98:3 says he hath remembered his mercy and his truth toward the house of Israel.

questions.question: Who have seen the salvation of our God according to Psalms 98:3?
options: All the ends of the earth
questions.correctAnswer: All the ends of the earth
questions.explanation: Psalms 98:3 states that all the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 98:1 commands singing unto the LORD an old song.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 98:1 specifically says to sing unto the LORD a new song, not an old song.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD's righteousness is shown openly to the heathen according to Psalms 98:2.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 98:2 says his righteousness hath he openly shewed in the sight of the heathen.

questions.question: What is the first instruction given in Psalms 98 regarding praising the LORD?
options: Sing unto the LORD a new song
questions.correctAnswer: Sing unto the LORD a new song
questions.explanation: Psalms 98:1 begins with the instruction to sing unto the LORD a new song before other commands appear.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 98:3 says the LORD has forgotten his mercy toward the house of Israel.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 98:3 says he hath remembered his mercy and his truth toward the house of Israel, not forgotten it.

questions.question: Which body parts are mentioned in Psalms 98:1 as instruments of victory?
questions.correctAnswer: Right hand and holy arm
questions.explanation: Psalms 98:1 mentions the LORD's right hand, and his holy arm, hath gotten him the victory.

questions.question: What should all the earth do according to Psalms 98:4?
options: Make a joyful noise, rejoice, and sing praise
questions.correctAnswer: Make a joyful noise, rejoice, and sing praise
questions.explanation: Psalms 98:4 commands all the earth to make a joyful noise unto the LORD, rejoice, and sing praise.

questions.question: According to Psalms 98:5, with what instruments are we told to sing unto the LORD?
options: Harp and voice of a psalm
questions.correctAnswer: Harp and voice of a psalm
questions.explanation: Psalms 98:5 says sing unto the LORD with the harp; with the harp, and the voice of a psalm.

questions.question: According to Psalms 98:6, what instruments are used to make a joyful noise before the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: Trumpets and sound of cornet
questions.explanation: Psalms 98:6 instructs to make a joyful noise before the LORD with trumpets and sound of cornet.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 98:9 tells us the LORD will judge the world with righteousness and equity.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 98:9 states the LORD cometh to judge the earth, and with righteousness shall he judge the world, and the people with equity.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 98 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 98 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 98:4, what are all the earth called to do before the LORD?
options: Make a joyful noise, rejoice, and sing praise
questions.correctAnswer: Make a joyful noise, rejoice, and sing praise
questions.explanation: Psalms 98:4 specifically commands all the earth to make a joyful noise, rejoice, and sing praise to the LORD, emphasizing wholehearted worship.

questions.question: How does Psalms 98:5 instruct believers to sing unto the LORD?
options: With the harp and the voice of a psalm
questions.correctAnswer: With the harp and the voice of a psalm
questions.explanation: Verse 5 directs singing unto the LORD with the harp and the voice of a psalm, highlighting musical praise combined with vocal expression.

questions.question: What instruments are mentioned in Psalms 98:6 to make a joyful noise before the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: Trumpets and sound of cornet
questions.explanation: Psalms 98:6 specifies trumpets and the sound of the cornet as instruments to make a joyful noise before the LORD, emphasizing celebratory worship with brass instruments.

questions.question: What biblical virtue is exemplified by the instruction in Psalms 98:4-6 to make a joyful noise and sing praise with instruments?
options: Joyful worship and gratitude toward God
questions.correctAnswer: Joyful worship and gratitude toward God
questions.explanation: These verses encourage expressing joy and gratitude through loud, musical praise, illustrating the virtue of joyful worship and thankfulness to God (Psalms 98:4-6).

questions.question: What does Psalms 98:6 teach us about the nature of God as King and how we should respond?
options: We should make a joyful noise before the LORD, the King
We should remain silent and fear Him
We should hide from His judgment
We should only praise Him quietly
questions.correctAnswer: We should make a joyful noise before the LORD, the King
questions.explanation: Verse 6 calls the LORD 'the King' and commands joyful noise before Him, showing reverence through celebratory praise acknowledging His sovereign rule.

questions.question: How does Psalms 98:5-6 together encourage believers in their worship practices?
options: By combining vocal praise with instrumental music to express joy
By forbidding the use of instruments
By focusing solely on personal meditation
questions.correctAnswer: By combining vocal praise with instrumental music to express joy
questions.explanation: Verses 5 and 6 together instruct singing with the harp and voice, plus joyful noise with trumpets and cornet, blending vocal and instrumental worship in joyful praise.

questions.question: What will happen if, according to Psalms 98:4, all the earth makes a joyful noise, rejoices, and sings praise?
options: There will be universal celebration of God's salvation
questions.correctAnswer: There will be universal celebration of God's salvation
questions.explanation: The command to all the earth to joyfully praise God leads into verses describing creation’s joyful response to God's salvation, indicating universal celebration (Psalms 98:4-7).

questions.question: A believer struggling with joy in worship is encouraged by Psalms 98:4-6 to do what?
options: Express worship through joyful noise, singing, and instruments
Remain silent and pray privately only
Avoid music and focus on reading scripture
Wait for feelings of joy before praising
questions.correctAnswer: Express worship through joyful noise, singing, and instruments
questions.explanation: These verses instruct making joyful noise, singing, and playing instruments before the LORD, teaching that worship includes active, joyful expression regardless of feelings.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 98:5 teaches that singing unto the LORD should be done only silently without instruments.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 98:5 explicitly mentions singing unto the LORD with the harp and the voice of a psalm, indicating instrumental accompaniment, not silence.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 98:6, making a joyful noise with trumpets and cornet is a way to honor the LORD as King.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 6 calls for joyful noise with trumpets and cornet before the LORD, the King, showing that musical celebration honors His kingship.

questions.question: What does Psalms 98:4-6 imply about the relationship between joy and obedience in worship?
options: Joyful worship with singing and instruments is an act of obedience
Joy is optional and not linked to worship
questions.correctAnswer: Joyful worship with singing and instruments is an act of obedience
questions.explanation: The command to make joyful noise and sing with instruments shows that expressing joy in worship is an obedient response to God's salvation (Psalms 98:4-6).

questions.question: How does the command in Psalms 98:6 to make a joyful noise before the LORD, the King, teach humility and reverence in worship?
options: By recognizing God's sovereignty and responding with joyful praise
By demanding silence and fear only
questions.correctAnswer: By recognizing God's sovereignty and responding with joyful praise
questions.explanation: The verse honors God as King, teaching worshipers to humbly acknowledge His rule and express reverence through joyful noise.

questions.question: What does Psalms 98:5 teach about the use of music in prayer and worship?
options: Music, such as harp and psalms, is a fitting accompaniment to vocal praise
Music should be avoided in worship
Only drums are acceptable for worship
Music should be played without singing
questions.correctAnswer: Music, such as harp and psalms, is a fitting accompaniment to vocal praise
questions.explanation: Verse 5 pairs the harp with the voice of a psalm, showing that instrumental music supports vocal praise during worship.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 98:4-6 emphasize that worship should be a communal and expressive celebration involving all creation.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: These verses call all the earth to rejoice and make joyful noise with singing and instruments, indicating communal and expressive worship (Psalms 98:4-6).

questions.question: What does Psalms 98:4 promise will happen if the earth makes a joyful noise and sings praise, as described in verses 7-9?
options: The sea, floods, and hills will also join in joyful celebration
questions.correctAnswer: The sea, floods, and hills will also join in joyful celebration
questions.explanation: Verses 7-9 describe creation's joyful response—sea roaring, floods clapping, hills rejoicing—following the earth's call to praise in verse 4.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 98 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 98.

questions.question: According to Psalms 98:7, what is called upon to roar?
questions.correctAnswer: The sea
questions.explanation: Psalms 98:7 explicitly states, 'Let the sea roar, and the fulness thereof.' Thus, it is the sea that is called upon to roar.

questions.question: What natural elements are personified as clapping their hands in Psalms 98:8?
questions.correctAnswer: The floods
questions.explanation: In Psalms 98:8 it says, 'Let the floods clap their hands,' personifying the floods as expressing joy by clapping.

questions.question: What is the reason given in Psalms 98:9 for the earth and its inhabitants to be joyful?
options: Because the LORD cometh to judge the earth
questions.correctAnswer: Because the LORD cometh to judge the earth
questions.explanation: Psalms 98:9 states, 'Before the LORD; for he cometh to judge the earth,' which is the reason for rejoicing mentioned.

questions.question: Which instruments are mentioned in Psalms 98:6 to make a joyful noise before the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: Trumpets and cornet
questions.explanation: Psalms 98:6 specifies 'With trumpets and sound of cornet make a joyful noise before the LORD.'

questions.question: What is the LORD's manner of judgment described in Psalms 98:9?
questions.correctAnswer: Judging with righteousness and equity
questions.explanation: Psalms 98:9 explains that the LORD will 'judge the world, and the people with equity,' emphasizing righteousness and fairness.

questions.question: Which phrase in Psalms 98:3 reflects God's faithfulness to Israel?
options: He hath remembered his mercy and his truth toward the house of Israel
He hath made a new covenant with the heathen
He hath forgotten not the Gentiles
He hath delivered all the kings
questions.correctAnswer: He hath remembered his mercy and his truth toward the house of Israel
questions.explanation: Psalms 98:3 states God 'hath remembered his mercy and his truth toward the house of Israel,' highlighting His ongoing faithfulness.

questions.question: What literary device is most evident in Psalms 98:7-9 where natural elements join in praise and judgment?
questions.correctAnswer: Personification
questions.explanation: Natural elements like the sea roaring and floods clapping their hands (Psalms 98:7-8) show personification, attributing human actions to nature.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of God judging the earth with righteousness as in Psalms 98:9?
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 96:13
questions.explanation: Psalm 96:13 speaks of the LORD coming to judge the earth with righteousness, similar to Psalms 98:9, connecting the theme of divine judgment.

questions.question: Which New Testament verse reflects the theme of singing a new song as in Psalms 98:1?
questions.correctAnswer: Revelation 5:9
questions.explanation: Revelation 5:9 mentions singing a new song to the Lamb, echoing the call in Psalms 98:1 to sing a new song for marvelous deeds.

questions.question: The Hebrew word translated as 'salvation' in Psalms 98:2 primarily means:
questions.correctAnswer: Deliverance or victory
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'salvation' (yeshu‘ah) in Psalms 98:2 emphasizes deliverance or victory, fitting the context of God's mighty acts.

questions.question: How does Psalms 98:4-6 develop the theme of communal worship?
options: By calling all the earth to make joyful noise with instruments and singing
By instructing only the priests to sing
questions.correctAnswer: By calling all the earth to make joyful noise with instruments and singing
questions.explanation: Verses 4-6 invite all the earth to rejoice with loud noise, singing, harp, trumpets, and cornets, highlighting communal joyous worship.

questions.question: What does the 'right hand' and 'holy arm' symbolize in Psalms 98:1?
questions.correctAnswer: God's power and victory
questions.explanation: In Psalms 98:1, 'his right hand, and his holy arm' symbolize God's mighty power and victorious acts.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 98 calls upon the hills to be joyful together in response to God's coming judgment.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 98:8 says, 'let the hills be joyful together before the LORD,' linking natural rejoicing with God's coming judgment in verse 9.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 98:3 states that only the house of Israel has seen the salvation of God.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 98:3 says 'all the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God,' indicating universal revelation, not just Israel.

questions.question: Which theme found in Psalms 98:7-9 is also a prominent motif in the prophetic books concerning the Day of the LORD?
options: The cosmic disturbance and divine judgment
questions.correctAnswer: The cosmic disturbance and divine judgment
questions.explanation: Psalms 98:7-9 depicts nature reacting to God's coming judgment, a common motif in prophets like Joel (Joel 3:16) describing the Day of the LORD.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 98 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 98 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is primarily demonstrated by the LORD's 'right hand' and 'holy arm' obtaining victory, as mentioned in Psalms 98:1?
questions.correctAnswer: God's omnipotence
questions.explanation: Psalms 98:1 describes God's right hand and holy arm gaining victory, symbolizing His all-powerful ability to achieve triumph, which reveals His omnipotence.

questions.question: According to Psalms 98:2, what has the LORD made known openly before the heathen?
questions.correctAnswer: His salvation and righteousness
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly states that the LORD has made known His salvation and openly shown His righteousness before the heathen, emphasizing divine justice and redemptive act.

questions.question: Which doctrine is highlighted by the LORD remembering 'his mercy and his truth toward the house of Israel' as stated in Psalms 98:3?
questions.correctAnswer: The covenant faithfulness of God
questions.explanation: Psalms 98:3 reveals God's mercy and truth towards Israel, underscoring His covenant faithfulness, a key doctrine that God remains true to His promises to His people.

questions.question: What universal response to God's salvation does Psalms 98:4 exhort all the earth to perform?
options: Make a joyful noise, rejoice, and sing praise
questions.correctAnswer: Make a joyful noise, rejoice, and sing praise
questions.explanation: Verse 4 calls for a loud, joyful response from all the earth, emphasizing praise and rejoicing as appropriate responses to God's salvation.

questions.question: What instruments are specifically mentioned in Psalms 98:5 as means to sing unto the LORD?
options: Harp and voice of a psalm
questions.correctAnswer: Harp and voice of a psalm
questions.explanation: Psalms 98:5 commands singing unto the LORD with the harp and the voice of a psalm, indicating the use of stringed instruments and vocal praise.

questions.question: How does Psalms 98:6 describe the sound made before the LORD, the King?
options: With trumpets and the sound of the cornet making a joyful noise
questions.correctAnswer: With trumpets and the sound of the cornet making a joyful noise
questions.explanation: The verse specifies trumpets and cornet sounds to make joyful noise before the LORD, emphasizing celebratory and regal worship.

questions.question: What theological truth can be drawn from the call for the sea and all who dwell therein to roar in Psalms 98:7?
questions.correctAnswer: Creation's universal praise of God
questions.explanation: Verse 7 invites the sea and its fullness to roar, symbolizing that all creation participates in praising God, affirming the doctrine of creation's response to the Creator.

questions.question: What is the significance of the floods clapping their hands and the hills being joyful together in Psalms 98:8?
options: It represents nature rejoicing in God's righteous judgment
It symbolizes natural disasters punishing sinners
It foretells the end of the world
questions.correctAnswer: It represents nature rejoicing in God's righteous judgment
questions.explanation: The verse poetically shows nature rejoicing, indicating harmony in creation in response to God's righteous judgment, highlighting God's justice and sovereignty.

questions.question: According to Psalms 98:9, with what qualities will the LORD judge the world and the people?
questions.correctAnswer: Righteousness and equity
questions.explanation: Psalms 98:9 declares that God will judge the earth with righteousness and the people with equity, affirming God's just and fair nature in judgment.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal truth about God's salvation and judgment is conveyed by Psalms 98:3 and Psalms 98:9 together?
options: God remembers mercy toward Israel and judges the earth with righteousness
God judges the earth with wrath and forgets His covenant
God saves only Israel and condemns the nations
questions.correctAnswer: God remembers mercy toward Israel and judges the earth with righteousness
questions.explanation: Verse 3 shows God's covenant mercy toward Israel, while verse 9 emphasizes His righteous judgment over all earth, combining to teach God's mercy and justice coexist in salvation history.

questions.question: How do Psalms 98:5-6 together illustrate the nature of worship appropriate to God as King?
options: Joyful, musical, and celebratory worship using instruments and voices
questions.correctAnswer: Joyful, musical, and celebratory worship using instruments and voices
questions.explanation: Verses 5 and 6 command singing with harp, psalms, trumpets, and cornet, indicating exuberant, musical worship befitting God's kingship.

questions.question: What does the universal call to 'all the earth' in Psalms 98:4 and the inclusion of 'all the ends of the earth' in Psalms 98:3 signify about the scope of God's salvation?
options: God's salvation is universal and intended for all peoples
God's salvation is limited to Israel only
God's salvation excludes those in distant lands
questions.correctAnswer: God's salvation is universal and intended for all peoples
questions.explanation: Verse 3 states all ends of the earth have seen God's salvation; verse 4 calls all the earth to rejoice, showing salvation's universal scope, consistent with biblical redemption narrative.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Psalms 98 portrays God as a harsh judge lacking mercy. What does Psalms 98:1-3 actually teach about God's character?
options: God is merciful, truthful, and victorious in salvation
God is only a judge with no mercy
God is indifferent to human affairs
God is constrained by human sin
questions.correctAnswer: God is merciful, truthful, and victorious in salvation
questions.explanation: Verses 1-3 emphasize God's marvelous works, salvation, mercy, and truth toward Israel, showing a God who is both just and merciful, not harsh without compassion.

questions.question: What theological insight is gained by combining Psalms 98:7-8 about creation's joyful response with Psalms 98:9 about God's righteous judgment?
options: Creation rejoices because God's judgment establishes justice and order
Creation fears destruction from God's judgment
Creation is indifferent to God's actions
questions.correctAnswer: Creation rejoices because God's judgment establishes justice and order
questions.explanation: Verses 7-8 depict nature rejoicing, while verse 9 explains God judges with righteousness; together they show creation's harmony arises from God's just governance.

questions.question: How does Psalms 98:2-3 demonstrate the relationship between God's righteousness and His covenant promises in the grand narrative of redemption?
options: God's righteousness is revealed openly as He fulfills His covenant mercy to Israel
God's covenant promises are conditional and rarely fulfilled
God hides His righteousness from the nations
questions.correctAnswer: God's righteousness is revealed openly as He fulfills His covenant mercy to Israel
questions.explanation: Verse 2 reveals God's righteousness openly; verse 3 recalls His mercy and truth to Israel, together affirming God's faithfulness in the redemption story.
